name: Heritable Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension due to BMPR2 Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) Guidelines for Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure ≥25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure ≤15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of pathogenic BMPR2 gene mutation confirmed by genetic testing
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as connective tissue disease or chronic thromboembolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic criteria met by right heart catheterization plus confirmed BMPR2 mutation and exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic counseling is recommended for patients and family members.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output

pathognomonic.notes: Transient loss of consciousness during physical activity

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to hepatomegaly or ascites

occasional.notes: Vasospasm of extremities triggered by cold or stress

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests secondary to congestion
imaging: Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation on echocardiography
Pulmonary artery enlargement on chest CT or MRI
Perfusion defects excluded by ventilation-perfusion scan
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in BMPR2 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated pulmonary arterial pressure
Exclusion of secondary causes of pulmonary hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: Similar hemodynamic profile but no family history
Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure >15 mmHg
Echocardiographic evidence of left heart dysfunction

redFlags: Rapid progression of dyspnea and syncope
Signs of right heart failure such as peripheral edema and ascites
Sudden onset chest pain or hemoptysis
references: Simonneau G, Montani D, Celermajer DS, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019;53(1):1801913.
Machado RD, Southgate L, Eichstaedt CA, et al. Pulmonary arterial hypertension: a current perspective on established and emerging molecular genetic defects. Hum Mutat. 2015;36(12):1113-1127.
European Respiratory Society Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2022;60(1):2102768.
